transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

On Indesit washer-dryers like your XWDE 96 series, clothes coming out cold and wet usually points to one of three things: a blocked airflow path (lint filter or condenser), an overloaded drum, or a failed heating element. Since the wash cycle works fine, we can rule out general motor issues. First, please check if the lint filter at the bottom front is clean; fluff buildup stops hot air from circulating even if the heater works. Second, during the drying cycle, does the inside of the drum feel warm or hot to touch? If it's cold, the heater isn't working. If it's hot but clothes are still wet, it’s likely an airflow blockage or that you’ve put too much laundry in for a drying load (drying capacity is usually about half the wash capacity).
The drum and door glass stay stone cold during drying. I haven't checked the lint filter yet, will do that now. Load is about 4kg.

Since the drum stays cold, we need to rule out airflow issues before assuming the heater has failed; a blocked filter can sometimes trigger safety cut-outs that stop heating entirely. Please check the lint filter at the bottom front (unplug first, use towels for water) and also locate the condenser panel inside the door—usually a small grille near the top or side of the drum opening. Are both clear of fluff and debris?

I'm not sure I've found the condenser panel you mean. I can hear water trickling at the back during the dry though. I haven't done the filter yet, will do it now. No burning smell or tripping, by the way.

The water trickling you hear is normal for an Indesit washer-dryer; it’s the pump moving condensed moisture out during the drying phase. However, because the drum stays cold, we need to rule out a safety cut-out triggered by blocked airflow before assuming the heater has failed. Remove it and rinse off any fluff. If there is a second grille or filter behind that same panel (the condenser), take that out too and rinse it clean. Let both dry completely before putting them back in, then try a drying cycle again to see if heat returns.

ok, I've done the filter now and rinsed it. Still can't find a separate condenser panel though. Also worth saying the dry stopped heating after I pulled the plug mid-cycle last week to get a shirt out. Should I try a dry cycle again?

Yes, please try another drying cycle. Since the drum is stone cold, the heating element isn't working or has been cut off by a safety device (thermal cut-out). This often happens if airflow was restricted previously, even if you've now cleaned the main filter. On Indesit washer-dryers, there is usually a second filter/condenser unit behind a small flap at the bottom front. Please check for this, clean it if present, and then run a cycle to see if heat returns.

I can't see any flap at the bottom front, just the filter I already rinsed. I'm not sure there's a second one on mine. Is it worth running the dry again anyway, or is there something else I should check?

Yes, it is worth trying again. Run a short drying cycle with the drum empty or just one towel. If the drum remains stone cold and there are no new error codes, the heating element has likely failed. On this model, that part is not user-replaceable without professional tools and safety checks, so you will need to call an engineer.
